newsitem.title: UK: British cancer sufferers to sue two tobacco firms.
newsitem.headline: British cancer sufferers to sue two tobacco firms.

text.p: Forty cancer sufferers are planning to sue two tobacco companies for failing to change their products to limit the dangers of smoking, their lawyers said on Friday.
For the first time in a case of this size in Britain the plantiffs, who have been denied legal aid, will be represented by lawyers working on a no-win, no-fee basis.

"These are cases which must and should be brought within the British legal system. It would be an outrage if because of the refusal of legal aid these people couldn't bring their case to court," Martyn Day, a lawyer representing the claimants, told BBC radio.
The cancer sufferers say Imperial Tobacco and Gallaher should have reduced levels of tar in cigarettes 40 years ago after doctors began saying that tar was causing cancer.
The tobacco companies argue that there is no proof that by reducing the tar levels in cigarettes these people would not have suffered from cancer.

Under the agreement, the lawyers will receive no fee if the cancer victims lose the case but could earn an estimated three million pounds ($4.7 million) in legal fees and a similar amount from the plantiffs if they are successful.
The cancer victims were denied a petition for legal aid in July on the grounds that the case was unlikely to succeed.

"In the last 40 years, hundreds of such cases have been brought against tobacco companies worldwide and none of them have resulted in any tobacco company paying any damages at all," a spokesman for Imperial Tobacco said.
Jeff Jeffery, of Gallaher which is a unit of American Brands of the United States, said: "The company's policy is not to comment on matters of litigation whether current or pending."
The first step in the legal action is expected within the next few weeks and the lawyers hope that the case will reach court sometime in the next two years.
